problem: Learning-based visuomotor navigation lacks a compact, effective memory representation; NeRF has been largely overlooked as a memory structure for navigation compared with implicit (recurrent/latent) and explicit (map/topological) memories.
motivation: Memory representations are essential for viable long-horizon navigation. NeRF offers a compact spatial representation that encodes both appearance and geometry, and could support pose estimation, accessibility mapping and waypoint rendering for task decomposition.
key_idea: Use an offline-built NeRF prior as navigation memory, giving one-shot pose and depth estimation from a query image, a density-based accessibility map, and waypoint estimation and rendering for a global planner that drives an imitation-learned local controller.
insight: Based only on the abstract: NeRF density can serve as a proxy for space occupancy, so a single scene representation supports localization, mapping and subgoal generation. The abstract reports advantages over implicit and explicit memory baselines and interpretability studies, but no specific ablations are available.
method: Derivative radiance field: enables one-shot pose and depth estimation from a single query image.
Geometric accessibility map: assumes density equals space occupancy and derives the map from an offline-constructed NeRF prior.
Global planner: decomposes long-term tasks by estimating waypoints and rendering them as subgoal images.
Local controller: an imitation-learned visuomotor policy that reaches each waypoint.

setting.backbone: NeRF prior (offline-built per scene) + imitation-learned visuomotor local controller
setting.training_data: Imitation learning demonstrations for the local controller and per-scene offline NeRF construction; scale not given in the abstract
setting.privileged: offline-constructed NeRF prior of the scene (pre-built map-like memory)

results: The abstract states that the pipeline outperforms recent implicit and explicit memory approaches in image-goal navigation, and it was also validated in real-world scenarios. No numbers are given.
limitations: Requires an offline-constructed NeRF for each scene, so it is not applicable to unseen environments without prior mapping.
Full details, benchmarks and quantitative results are unavailable because only the abstract was provided.
